header.name: Southern Cheyenne camp move, Indian Territory, 1870s (draft for consultation)
header.description: A draft diorama of a camp move: lodges with poles and doors, a travois loaded for the move, two horses, three people as placeholder forms. Not reviewed by the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes; not for display.

object.name: Camp move (draft)
object.description: Root group. A Southern Cheyenne camp move on a river terrace on the North Fork of the Canadian. Not reviewed by the tribes.

certainty.note: Flat river terrace. No site survey; the shape is generic.

operations.author: jimmy
operations.text: Display needs review by the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes (see research/consultation-plan.md). The whole camp is a draft until then.

operations.author: jimmy
operations.text: The lodge shapes, the pole angles, the door and how the cover is folded need checking against Cheyenne practice.

operations.author: jimmy
operations.text: The travois sizes and the load are approximate. Check the load and how it was packed.

operations.author: jimmy
operations.text: The horses are placeholder silhouettes in real proportions. Breed, tack and colour are not claimed. Check with consultants before any display.

operations.author: jimmy
operations.text: The people are placeholder forms only: no faces, hair detail, clothing or regalia. They must not stand in for real people. Review before any display.

operations.author: jimmy
operations.text: The bluff is invented to frame the camp. It has no source.

operations.author: jimmy
operations.text: The fire ring size is typical, and the cold ash is an assumption.

operations.author: jimmy
operations.text: The grass tufts are decoration; their size is not measured.
